                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# 5. Querying the Database - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://wasp.sh/docs/0.11.8/tutorial/queries)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Queries are used to read an entity, while actions are used to create, modify, and delete entities.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'// ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query getTasks {\n'[39m +
                      [32m' // Specifies where the implementation for the query function is.\n'[39m +
                      [32m' // Use `@server` to import files inside the `src/server` folder.\n'[39m +
                      [32m' fn: import { getTasks } from "@server/queries.js",\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'@wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'- ```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Notice how you don't need to annotate the type of the query's return value: Wasp uses the types you defined while implementing the query for the generated client-side function.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'This is **full-stack type safety**: the types on the client always match the types on the server.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# A dive into Wasp; a domain-specific language for building full stack ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2023-01-24, last updated: 2026-07-22, [Read more](https://blog.openreplay.com/a-dive-into-wasp/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Operations in Wasp are essentially two types: `queries`, which are for fetching items in your database, and `actions` for creating and updating your database.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do this, we have to describe it inside `main.wasp` by using the `query` keyword for queries and the `action` keyword for actions.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                      [32m'description String\n'[39m +
                      [32m'isDone Boolean @default(false)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'psl=}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'query getDuties { //for fetching duties from our database\n'[39m +
                      [32m'fn: import { getDuties } from "@server/queries.js",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'entities: [Duty]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Actions\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create an Action, you need to:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Declare the Action in Wasp using the\n'[39m +

                      [32m'action\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To create an Action in Wasp, we begin with an\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'). This function takes a single optional argument - an object containing any serializable data you wish to use inside the Action.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Wasp will send this object over the network and pass it into the Action's implementation as its first positional argument (more on this when we look at the implementations).\n"[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'First, you have to declare your query in the `main.wasp` file like so:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Your app fundamentals and features, such as authentication, database model, routes, page, operations, etc., are described with the Wasp DSL inside the main.wasp file, and the rest of your application is written in React and Node.js.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-migrate/workflows/seeding)\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Seeding Database Data | Prisma Cheat Sheet | Mapagam\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-29, last updated: 2026-08-03, [Read more](https://www.mapagam.com/backend/prisma/seeding-database-data/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## 1.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Creating Seed Script\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// prisma/seed.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const prisma = new PrismaClient();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'async function main() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'await prisma.user.upsert({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'where: { email: "admin@example.com" },\n'[39m +
                      [32m'update: {},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'create: { email: "admin@example.com", role: "ADMIN" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'main().finally(() => prisma.$disconnect());\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Aspect|Detail|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|--|--|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Idempotent|Use\n'[39m +
                      [32m'``` upsert ``` / skipDuplicates|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Order|Parents before children|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Configuring Seed Command\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"prisma": { "seed": "tsx prisma/seed.ts" }\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Runner|Use|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|tsx|Fast TypeScript runner|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|ts-node|Mature|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|node|For compiled JS|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## 3.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running Seed Command\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Command|Detail|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|--|--|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|``` prisma db seed ```|Manual execution|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|``` migrate reset ```|Auto-runs seed|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|``` migrate dev ```|Runs seed on first migration of empty DB|'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How do you seed a database with Prisma? - Benevolent Bytes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2022-08-03, last updated: 2026-07-07, [Read more](https://blog.sethcorker.com/question/how-do-you-seed-a-database-with-prisma/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The key things to in your seed script are:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Import the Prisma client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Create the records you want to seed in your DB using the client\n'[39m +
                      [32m'3. Await the creation of these records (otherwise node will terminate too soon)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* For each coffee name, create a Coffee record in the DB\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*/\n'[39m +
                      [32m'function seedCoffee() {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Promise.all(COFFEE_NAMES.map(n => prisma.coffee.create({ data: { name: n } })))\n'[39m +
                      [32m".then(() => console.info('[SEED] Succussfully create coffee records'))\n"[39m +
                      [32m".catch(e => console.error('[SEED] Failed to create coffee records', e))\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'seedCoffee();\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To tell Prisma that we have a seed, we need to add a property to our package.json:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"prisma": {\n'[39m +
